business_problem: Coinbase needed to eliminate passwords and long-lived certificates for MongoDB access because stored credentials, ghost accounts, and secrets-manager copies created exploitable security gaps as the exchange scaled.
solution_summary: Coinbase inserted a new certificate-based access layer in front of the MongoDB Atlas databases that support critical financial applications. Instead of letting employees and services authenticate with persistent usernames, passwords, or long-lived certificates, the company built an internal PKI system that generates unique credentials on demand whenever an approved user or workload needs Atlas access. Those certificates expire within minutes, so a leaked secret or stale account becomes useless after a session ends. Atlas remains the system of record for the operational data, while the PKI service orchestrates identity issuance in real time and removes the need to store reusable credentials in configuration files or secret managers. The design preserves the low-latency access the platform needs while aligning database authentication with Coinbase's zero-trust security posture.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores and serves the operational financial data that Coinbase applications access through the new certificate-based authentication flow.

solution_components.name: internal PKI system
solution_components.role: Generates ephemeral client certificates on demand so employees and services can connect to Atlas without stored credentials.

data_flow: When an approved employee or service needs database access, Coinbase's internal PKI system issues a short-lived certificate in real time, the caller uses that certificate to connect to MongoDB Atlas, and the credential becomes invalid automatically when the session ends or the expiration window closes.
business_outcome: Coinbase removed ghost accounts and persistent database secrets from a large share of its Atlas estate while maintaining subsecond access patterns for mission-critical workloads and setting up a stronger foundation for future encryption controls.
metrics: Coinbase has migrated approximately 50% of its traditional authentication system to the certificate-based framework.
Coinbase issues approximately 200,000 certificates daily—more than 80 million per year.
The platform maintains sub-50 millisecond latency.
Certificates can expire in as little as five minutes.
architecture_clues: Ephemeral certificates replace passwords and long-lived certificates for Atlas authentication.
Credentials are generated dynamically instead of being stored in secrets managers or configuration files.
The design is intended to support zero-trust security practices for database access.
